title: Conjecture 1.8
statement_text: For all integers $\kappa, \ell \geq 0$, there exists $c \geq 0$ such that every graph with chromatic number greater than $c$ contains either a complete subgraph on $\kappa$ vertices or holes of $\ell$ consecutive lengths.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. A hole is an induced cycle of length at least four, and holes of $\ell$ consecutive lengths means holes of lengths $k,k+1,\dots,k+\ell-1$ for some $k$. The authors previously proved that for every $\ell$ there is $c$ such that every triangle-free graph with chromatic number greater than $c$ contains holes of $\ell$ consecutive lengths, and conjectured in that earlier paper that the same holds when only $K_\kappa$ is excluded; this conjecture remains open. In this paper they prove that for all $\kappa,\ell$ there is $c$ such that every graph with $\chi(G)>c$ and $\omega(G)\le\kappa$ contains holes of every length modulo $\ell$ (implying Gyárfás's three conjectures on odd holes, long holes and long odd holes, and the Kalai–Meshulam conjecture proved by Bonamy, Charbit and Thomassé on holes of length divisible by three), and, as a small step towards this conjecture, that such graphs contain holes of two consecutive lengths, both of length more than $\ell$. They say they could get three consecutive long holes with a great deal of omitted work, but no more. Note that holes of a specific length cannot be forced, since there are graphs of arbitrarily large girth and chromatic number.
notes: Explicitly labelled 'Conjecture' in the paper. The authors state it was conjectured in their earlier paper [14]; the theorem header carries no parenthetical attribution, so classified as 'states' per schema rules. Theorem 1.9 of this paper (holes of two consecutive long lengths) is proved as a step towards this conjecture.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs of graphs with large chromatic number. X. Holes of specific residue
